root.name: Blackmar-Diemer Gambit Accepted: Ziegler Defense
root.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. e4 dxe4 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. f3 exf3 5. Nxf3 c6

overview: After 4.f3 exf3 5.Nxf3 c6 Black takes the pawn and prepares ...Bg4 or ...Bf5 and ...e6, aiming to hold the extra pawn with a solid pawn structure. White continues with Bc4, Bf4, O-O and Qe2, or Ne5 ideas, hoping for attack. Accurate defence gives Black the better game, but practical chances remain for White, especially at club level.

white_ideas.idea: Develop Bc4, Bf4 or Be3 and castle
Use the open f-file and Ne5 or g4 attacks
Aim at h7 and f7 with the queen and bishops

black_ideas.idea: Hold the pawn with ...Bg4 or ...Bf5, ...e6 and ...Nbd7
Trade queens and neutralise the attack

typical_structures.structure: Open centre with White d4 against Black c6 and e6 pawns
Black extra pawn with White ahead in development

character.notes: White attacks for a pawn with open lines and quick tactical chances.

gambit.notes: White gives the e-pawn for development and an attack, and Black can keep it.

soundness.notes: Engines judge the compensation insufficient after accurate defence; it works through traps and ease of attack.

structure.notes: The centre opens and the game turns on lines for pieces.

approach.notes: The BDG is seldom chosen by strong players but remains popular below master level.

level.notes: Attack patterns are simple but Black has to know defences; dubious so not for beginners.

sublines_that_differ.how: Black aims for ...e6 and ...Nbd7 with a solid hold on the pawn.
